text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Trust, currently in the Supreme Court to find out who holds its legal ownership with President Bakili Muluzi's government, has appointed new directors to its board.
- Members of Parliament yesterday barred the media in Mzuzu, northern Malawi, from a meeting to discuss a handbook guiding legislators in their constituencies.

- Government has suspended the operation of mini-buses by non-Malawians with immediate effect. Transport and Aviation Minister Harry Thomson said at a press conference in Blantyre that the Asian community was not exempted from the ban.
- Government has recently distributed 36 buses to businessmen in rural areas, a project initiated by the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) in 1992.
